claims.claim: The channeling of natural forces into the human world has shattered the purposefulness of the world where objects serve as the ends for tools and implements.
claims.supporting_excerpt: The channeling of natural forces into the human world has shattered the very purposefulness of the world, the fact that objects are the ends for which tools and implements are designed.

claims.claim: In the mode of production brought by automation, the traditional distinctions between operation and product, as well as the product's precedence over operation, have become obsolete.
claims.supporting_excerpt: In the mode of production ushered in by automation, the distinction between operation and product, as well as the product’s precedence over operation (which is only the means to produce the end), no longer make sense and have become obsolete.

definitions.definition: Things that are not made but grow by themselves into whatever they become, with an existence not separate from the process of coming into being.
Courses of movement which are self-moving and therefore outside the range of wilful and purposeful interference.

distinctions.distinction: Products of human hands must be realized step by step with a fabrication process entirely distinct from the fabricated thing's existence, whereas a natural thing's existence is identical with the process through which it comes into being.

must_not_be_lost: Automation shatters the purposefulness of the world and renders the distinction between operation and product obsolete.
The instrumentality of tools and implements relates to the object produced rather than exclusively to making human labor less painful.
parsed.segment_function: Examines automation, natural processes, and the transformation of the human world through technology, contrasting the purposefulness of the human artifice with the automatic character of natural processes and modern machinery.
